NextItNet preserves causality through left-only convolution padding: kernel width k and dilation d require (k−1)d zeros, followed by valid convolution. Normalization must operate across channels independently at each timestep; normalization across time can leak future information. Inspect every convolution’s actual dilation: RecBole’s two-convolution residual block uses d followed by 2d. [NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [implementation](https://www.recbole.io/docs/_modules/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/nextitnet.html).

Derived structural check: start with reachable offsets S={0}; each convolution updates S to {s+jd : s∈S, j=0,…,k−1}; residual branches union their offset sets. For stride-one stacks, maximum span is 1+Σ(k−1)d, but this alone does not establish that every intervening position is reachable. Channel-only normalization and pointwise layers preserve offsets. Test causality by changing positions after t and checking that features through t remain unchanged. Probe unreachable offsets separately; zero gradients at reachable positions can reflect inactive nonlinearities rather than absent connections.

Recommended deployment checks: with dropout disabled, compare full-sequence features at t against processing the identical prefix with matching padding/alignment. For these left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position—normally index −1—rather than nonpadding_count−1; Microsoft’s NextItNet inference implementation reads index −1. Finally, reload the saved checkpoint through the generated predictor and compare candidate scores with the training model and diagnostic adapter on identical histories. Adapter tests alone cannot establish predictor correctness: verify architecture, weights, routing, truncation, padding, item IDs and scoring parity. [Microsoft implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html).
